newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Japan patrol butts Taiwan protest boat-radio.
newsitem.headline: Japan patrol butts Taiwan protest boat-radio.

text.p: A Japanese patrol boat butted a Taiwan protest boat early on Monday near a disputed East China Sea island chain as a flotilla of anti-Japanese boats approached the archipelago for a landing, Taiwan state radio said.
"Japan's PS 108 intentionally butted the stern of my boat and we were slightly damaged," the captain of one of the vessels told the station by ship-to-shore radio.

A force of at least 20 to 30 Japanese coastal patrol vessels placed themselves between the fleet of about 50 Taiwan boats and the islands to prevent them from nearing the uninhabited archipelago, the radio reported.

No one was reported hurt. It was not known whether any of the more than 300 protesters from Taiwan and Hong Kong had boarded motorcycle-like waverunners and small rubber rafts brought for a planned landing attempt.
The reported incident was 13 miles from the islands claimed by Japan as the Senkakus and Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus.

Taiwan and Hong Kong activists began mounting landing attempts in September, pledging to remove Japan's flag and a lighthouse erected on one of the islands in July by a Japanese ultra-nationalist group in an assertion of Tokyo's sovereignty.
